skill_name: lo-fi hip-hop production recipe
producer_intent: A terse generative prompt renders only what it names. Spelling out the canonical lo-fi elements + production character makes the generated loop sound like the brief instead of a bare drum loop.
when: Generating a lo-fi / hip-hop beat or loop from a text prompt.

recipe.guidance: name every element + the production character: dusty boom-bap drums, warm Rhodes/electric-piano chords, mellow sub bass, plus vinyl crackle, tape saturation and MPC swing; reference 90s SP-1200/J Dilla; comma-separated tags with BPM + key

evidence.brief: lo-fi hip-hop beat, dusty boom-bap drums, warm Rhodes chords, mellow sub bass

skill_name: Dusty Boom-Bap Drums with MPC Swing
producer_intent: Add authentic boom-bap drum texture with the signature swing of an MPC sampler to make the beat feel loose and vintage.
when: when generating the drum loop via prompt

skill_name: Mellow Sub Bass with Vintage Tape Saturation
producer_intent: Add a gentle, round sub bass that sits underneath the beat, colored with vintage tape warmth for that lo-fi character.
when: when generating the bass line via prompt

recipe.guidance: mellow sub bass, vintage tape saturation

skill_name: Boom-bap drum pattern (kick/snare/8th-hats)
producer_intent: the classic boom-bap skeleton — kick on the 1 and the 'and' of 3, snare on the 2 & 4, hats on every 8th
when: programming a boom-bap or lo-fi hip-hop drum pattern from scratch

skill_name: MPC swing on the hats (~0.58)
producer_intent: push the off-beat 8ths late for that drunk MPC/boom-bap swing instead of a stiff straight grid
when: the hats/drums feel too straight and need a swung, off-grid groove

skill_name: Humanize the keys (subtle timing + velocity)
producer_intent: a small seeded timing + velocity jitter so a programmed Rhodes/keys part breathes instead of sounding robotic
when: a programmed keys/chord part sounds too quantized / robotic

skill_name: Filter-open automation over the intro
producer_intent: automate the EQ/filter opening up over the bars for movement, instead of a single static setting
when: an intro/build needs movement — open the filter up over time

skill_name: Shared reverb on a send bus
producer_intent: send the keys to ONE shared reverb return for depth, instead of a reverb inserted on every track
when: the mix needs depth / space — a shared reverb the tracks send to

skill_name: 808 boom with core trap drum skeleton
producer_intent: Lock in a sparse but heavy 2-bar drum foundation with booming kick placement, backbeat snare/clap, and enough space for the sub to hit hard.
when: Use as the main drum loop before adding variations and fills.

skill_name: key filter sweep into drop
producer_intent: Use the existing key filter to create a tension lift into the hook by opening the top end gradually.
when: Place on a 4- or 8-bar pre-drop phrase to make the arrangement breathe.

skill_name: dark space bus for keys
producer_intent: Send the keys to a shared return so the sparse harmony feels wider and more cinematic without cluttering the center.
when: Use when the keys feel too dry or too upfront in the mix.

skill_name: 808 and drum anchor pattern with snare discipline
producer_intent: Build a cleaner, hook-friendly drum pattern that emphasizes the downbeat, backbeat, and a few syncopated punches for the 808 to answer.
when: Use as an alternate section or chorus drum variation to keep the beat from looping too predictably.

skill_name: 90s boom bap one-two drum foundation with ghost-note variation
producer_intent: Build a simple kick/snare backbone, then add low-velocity ghost notes and slight off-grid placement for bounce.
when: When starting a boom bap beat and wanting a very simple, universal drum pocket with swing.

skill_name: Basic boom bap hat pocket with light swing
producer_intent: Keep hats simple but give them a small amount of swing so the groove feels less rigid.
when: When programming a straight hat line and wanting the classic relaxed boom bap bounce.

skill_name: Drum groove programming with kick layering around a break
producer_intent: Program a simple boom-bap drum pocket by placing kicks on the main backbeat while keeping a spare, punchier feel.
when: When the beat needs extra punch layered over a drum break and the kicks should lock into the groove rather than sound rigid.

skill_name: Swinging programmed hats instead of hard quantization
producer_intent: Keep the hats loose and musical by applying swing to a straight hat grid instead of forcing rigid timing.
when: When a hat part already exists on 8ths and you want the tutorial-style swung feel without perfectly straight timing.

skill_name: Humanizing a simple melodic part to keep it behind the beat
producer_intent: Introduce small deterministic timing/velocity variation so the keys feel played rather than fully grid-locked.
when: When the arp or melodic line should sit a little behind the pocket and avoid sounding robotic.

skill_name: Filter automation to create movement in a loopy sample
producer_intent: Automate the EQ filter frequency to make the loop move and create section contrast without changing notes.
when: When the arrangement needs a simple rise/fall movement from the same loop, like bringing in variation across sections.

skill_name: Shared ambience send for glue and section cohesion
producer_intent: Route the keys into a shared return so the loop sits in a common space and feels more glued together.
when: When the beat needs subtle space and cohesion rather than a dry, isolated loop.

skill_name: Program a simple boom-bap kick/snare backbeat
producer_intent: Lay down the core drum pocket with kick on beats 1 and 3 and snare on beats 2 and 4.
when: After the sample chops are in place and before adding hats/open hats.

skill_name: Add swing to straight eighth-note hats
producer_intent: Turn rigid hats into a looser pocket by applying swing to the straight eighth-note grid.
when: After the hat line is programmed and needs a more human, sampled feel.

skill_name: Humanize a programmed keys part
producer_intent: Make the keys/arp feel less robotic by adding small deterministic timing and velocity variation.
when: After the keys arp is in place and before finalizing the loop feel.

skill_name: Humanize programmed MIDI for a natural piano feel
producer_intent: Make a played-in piano part feel less robotic by adding deterministic timing and velocity variation.
when: Use after entering or copying a MIDI piano part that was manually played and needs more human feel.

skill_name: Quantize straight hats into a swung boom-bap pocket
producer_intent: Turn straight 8th-note hats into a swung feel to better match a gritty boom-bap groove.
when: Use on the hats clip after programming or importing straight hats.

skill_name: Build a sparse boom-bap drum backbeat
producer_intent: Program the core kick/snare backbone with a simple two-hit kick and backbeat snare pattern.
when: Use as the foundational drum loop before layering other elements.

skill_name: layer_kick_into_drum_break
producer_intent: Add punch and low-end to a drum break by layering a complementary kick on the main backbeats so the drums knock harder without fighting the sample.
when: When a drum break feels good but needs more punch and low-end body.

skill_name: swing_hats_to_match_break_feel
producer_intent: Reprogram straight hats with swing so they move with the sample and drum break instead of sounding rigid.
when: When the hats need subtle movement and the groove should feel more human and pocketed.

skill_name: humanize_sample_style_melodic_part
producer_intent: Add small timing and velocity variation to a programmed melodic part so it feels less robotic and more like a played sample chop or live performance.
when: When a MIDI melody or chop needs human feel and imperfect timing.

skill_name: simple boom-bap drum programming
producer_intent: Lay down a minimal, hard-hitting kick/snare pocket with the classic boom-bap backbeat.
when: After the melody is established and you want the drums to lock in without overcrowding the beat.

skill_name: hat swing programming
producer_intent: Turn straight 8th hats into a looser boom-bap pocket by adding swing to the hat grid.
when: When hats feel too rigid and you want a more human, head-nod swing.

skill_name: melody humanization for sloppy texture
producer_intent: Humanize a programmed melodic part so it feels played loosely and less robotic.
when: After programming a melodic loop and before committing it as a rough, gritty texture.

skill_name: filter sweep automation
producer_intent: Create movement by automating a filter parameter up over time, useful for bringing a layer in or opening it up in sections.
when: When you want a repeated melodic layer to evolve across the arrangement instead of staying static.

skill_name: shared send effects setup
producer_intent: Route a track to a shared aux bus for glue, space, or parallel processing.
when: When you want one layer to share a common effect path with other elements or get extra ambience without inserting it directly on the track.

skill_name: Finger-drummed kick/snare boom-bap bounce
producer_intent: Program a loose kick/snare backbone by playing freely instead of rigidly quantizing, so the groove feels more human and bounce-focused.
when: When building the main drum pocket after the melody is set.

skill_name: Swinged hat programming for behind-the-grid feel
producer_intent: Keep the hat loop from feeling robotic by pushing it into a swung 8th-note pocket.
when: When the first hat layer needs more movement and human feel.

skill_name: Melodic texture change-up with humanized timing
producer_intent: Make the repeated musical phrase feel less static by slightly humanizing timing and velocity, matching the tutorial's emphasis on subtle movement.
when: When adding variation to repeated chops/keys so the section feels less repetitive.

skill_name: Filter sweep for section change-up
producer_intent: Automate the keys filter to create an obvious section contrast and a subtle texture shift, like the tutorial's filtered duplicate layer/change-up.
when: When moving into a second half of a hook or another arrangement section that needs more texture.

skill_name: Shared ambience send for glue
producer_intent: Send the keys to a shared bus to create cohesion and add space, like a common ambience return in a polished beat.
when: When the keys need shared reverb/delay style depth in the arrangement.

skill_name: humanized off-grid glockenspiel feel
producer_intent: make a melodic MIDI part feel sloppy, swung, and performed rather than rigid
when: when programming the glockenspiel-style melodic line

skill_name: boom bap drum break programming
producer_intent: lay down a simple kick-and-snare pocket typical of chopped drum-break feel
when: when building the drums on the empty drum clip

skill_name: shared ambience send for melodic glue
producer_intent: route a melodic layer to a shared return for space and cohesion
when: when the keys/synth layer needs shared ambience

skill_name: drum-break style pocket programming
producer_intent: Program a simple kick/snare boom-bap pattern that leaves space and locks to the groove rather than overfilling the bar.
when: When you need a basic head-nod drum pattern under a grimy loop.

skill_name: program a sparse boom-bap drum break
producer_intent: Build a minimal kick/snare pocket that supports a one-chord melodic loop with bounce.
when: Use this after the melodic loop is established and you want the drums to lock the groove in.

skill_name: add subtle hat movement with swing
producer_intent: Take straight hats and introduce a loose swung feel to add momentum and make the beat feel less rigid.
when: Use this on a programmed hat layer once the drums feel too straight or static.

skill_name: humanize a keyboard part for natural feel
producer_intent: Make a repeated keyboard figure feel played by a human instead of perfectly grid-locked.
when: Use this after the keys line is written and you want a looser pocket without changing the notes themselves.

skill_name: Level drums by starting with kick, then bring in snare and the rest while leaving headroom
producer_intent: Set drum balance from the loudest anchor first so the beat knocks without clipping or eating headroom.
when: When the drum clip is already programmed and you want the mix to hit harder before adding melodies/bass.

skill_name: Swing straight hats to give boom-bap groove
producer_intent: Turn rigid straight hats into a laid-back pocket using swung 8ths.
when: When the hat loop feels too robotic and needs bounce without changing the core rhythm.

skill_name: Humanize melodic MIDI for a less robotic feel
producer_intent: Add small timing and velocity variation to a programmed arp so it feels performed rather than grid-locked.
when: When the keys/arp loop sounds too mechanical after programming.

skill_name: Create a shared aux send for keys ambience
producer_intent: Route the keys to a shared bus so ambience can be blended without inserting an effect directly on the source.
when: When the keys need shared parallel space or delay while staying in the beat mix.

skill_name: Automate key filter cutoff for movement
producer_intent: Use an EQ filter sweep to open or close the tonal space of the keys over time.
when: When the tutorial-style move is to add some motion to a static melody or chop using EQ automation.

skill_name: boom bap hat swing programming
producer_intent: Push straight 8th-note hats behind the beat to create human bounce and loosen the groove.
when: After laying in straight 8th-note hats and wanting them to feel less robotic.

skill_name: boom bap kick-snare grid
producer_intent: Program a simple backbeat with kick on beats 1 and 3 and snare on 2 and 4.
when: When building the core drum pattern from scratch.
